A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same research despite the changed title. However, v1 includes supplementary Sections 6–10, whereas v2 ends at the references and refers to supplementary material absent from the supplied PDF. This limits comparison of supplementary evidence and details.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark results, a 50-participant user study, component ablations, and supplementary analyses comparing evaluation metrics with human judgments.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark, user-study and ablation results, and adds an unfiltered-data ablation and qualitative storyboarding demonstrations.

M1.justification: V2 adds an application pipeline that follows scene generation with Qwen Image Edit identity replacement. The core backbone, correspondence masks and attention regularizer remain unchanged. Section 3.4 reformulates the stated training objective as flow matching; the PDFs do not establish that the original experiments were retrained.

E1.justification: The training sources, DL3DV-10K comparison and principal scene–prompt benchmark are retained. V2 adds demonstrated multi-frame storyboarding requiring both scene and actor identity consistency, distinct from v1's supplementary account of Kling video interpolation using generated keyframes.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains Qwen-Image-Edit, FLUX.1 Kontext Dev and SceneDecorator. Table 3 adds the 'ours w/o filter' comparison model alongside the retained DL3DV-10K-trained baseline and full model.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a filtered-versus-unfiltered training control and a two-stage storyboarding demonstration. The principal benchmark remains 425 scenes and 2,125 prompts, with the same metrics, 50 participants, three annotators per pair, and stated training and inference budgets. Newly disclosed filtering and sampling details do not establish changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: V2 definitely adds a MINIMA-filtering ablation and a storyboarding case study while retaining the attention-loss and DL3DV-10K ablations. However, v1's supplementary metric-validation analyses and compositing-error study cannot be matched against the unavailable v2 supplement, preventing a reliable assessment of the full extent of analytical changes.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-seed experiments, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The retained result tables still report point estimates, and both versions specify three annotators per scene–prompt pair.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the shared Table 3 rows are numerically unchanged. V2 adds unfiltered-data scores of 9.648 G2.5F-SA and 9.079 G2.5F-TIA, plus storyboard outputs. V1's supplementary metric–human agreement results and additional qualitative findings have no supplied v2 counterpart, leaving the overall extent of result changes uncertain.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 replaces the generic weighted noise-prediction formulation with explicit linear interpolation, a target velocity and a flow-matching objective. The correspondence-mask and attention-loss mathematics remain equivalent across versions; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim reference-scene/text-conditioned generation, a scene-consistent data pipeline, cross-view attention regularization, and superior scene/text alignment. 'Scene Staging' and 'correspondence-guided attention' reframe the existing task and contribution without materially changing their scientific scope.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges that the core model does not preserve foreground identity and requires a separate replacement stage. It also adds interpretations linking filtering to reduced structural drift and SceneDecorator's failures to reliance on raw visual similarity, while attributing user-study gains to both data construction and attention regularization.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies MINIMA's RoMa basis, a threshold exceeding 2,000 robust inliers, sampling that favors later video frames, and identity-replacement postprocessing. V1 supplies exact evaluator prompts, randomized select-all annotation instructions, majority filtering and alpha=0.8 vote aggregation. Their retention or revision cannot be checked because v2's referenced supplement is unavailable.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially repositioned around image editing, inpainting and consistent storytelling, replacing the earlier dedicated 3D-reconstruction discussion. V2 adds works including ACE++, Infinite-Story, StoryMaker and RoMa, and changes the SceneDecorator comparison from a distinction between tasks to a proposed limitation of training-free attention sharing.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title and terminology, extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction and related work around stage/actor storytelling, and reorganizes the data-pipeline explanation around three requirements. Experiments are restructured into evaluation setup, combined comparisons, ablations and an application section.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout. V2 rearranges the teaser, substantially redraws the framework diagram, places the ablation tables side by side, and adds the storyboard figure. The main qualitative-comparison images and attention-map examples are retained with resizing, relocation or relabeling.

improvement.justification: V2 improves task framing, specifies flow matching and filtering more clearly, adds a useful filtering ablation, and acknowledges the identity-preservation limitation. However, v1's metric-validation evidence and detailed evaluation instructions are unavailable in the supplied v2 despite continued supplementary references. This gap prevents a reliable judgment of whether the gains outweigh a loss of evidential support and reproducibility.
